score_100.reason: Fig. 4D primarily evaluates whether eomesa, pvalb7, and their co-expressing population are correctly localized in whole-brain anatomical coordinates, and whether this localization supports the biological interpretation of a hippocampus-homologous region and Purkinje-cell labeling. The three 3D whole-brain maps are the basis of the panel and are worth 30 points. Positivity thresholds, atlas registration, and consistency across three fish are methodological sources and are worth 15 points. The scientific interpretation is split into three parts: eomesa-pvalb7 co-expression in the dorsolateral pallium and its hippocampus-homology interpretation is worth 25 points; pvalb7 localization in cerebellar Purkinje cells and its dual regional distribution is worth 20 points; and the broader relationship between molecular identity and anatomical specialization, with appropriate limits on interpretation, is worth 10 points. Point allocation: graph 30, methods 15, co-expression localization 25, pvalb7 localization 20, overall meaning and boundaries 10.

rubric.GT core conclusion: Fig. 4D uses three sets of 3D whole-brain visualizations to show the spatial distributions of eomesa-positive, pvalb7-positive, and eomesa-pvalb7 co-expressing cells. eomesa-positive cells are mainly located in the telencephalon; pvalb7-positive cells are located along the lateral edge of the dorsal pallium and label Purkinje cells in the cerebellum; and co-expressing cells are concentrated in the dorsolateral pallium, the region homologous to the mammalian hippocampus. The figure shows that specific gene combinations can precisely anchor anatomically specialized neuronal populations, but the panel itself mainly provides spatial-localization evidence rather than functional causal evidence.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly analyzes and visualizes the 3D whole-brain spatial distributions of the three cell populations: eomesa-positive cells are primarily telencephalic, pvalb7-positive cells are distributed along the lateral dorsal pallium and in the cerebellum, and eomesa-pvalb7 co-expressing cells are concentrated in the dorsolateral pallium; the reproduction includes dorsal and lateral views, key anatomical contours, a 100 um scale bar, and spatial patterns consistent with the original figure.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct full points if the main brain-region distributions of the three populations are reversed or shown as nearly uniform whole-brain distributions. Deduct 10 points if either the dorsal or lateral view is missing. Deduct 8 points if the dorsal-pallium or cerebellar anatomical contour is missing. Deduct 5 points if scale-bar and spatial-orientation information are completely absent. Deduct full points if the panel is confused with a Delta F/F functional activity map, a connectome map, or a neuronal morphology reconstruction.

Scoring items.criterion: States that cell positivity is defined by EASI-FISH RNA spot-count thresholds, that co-expressing cells must meet the threshold for both eomesa and pvalb7, that cell coordinates are registered to the mapZebrain atlas, that distributional consistency across three fish supports reproducible localization, and that color or point intensity represents mRNA spot count rather than functional activity.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 6 points if RNA spot-count thresholding or positivity definition is not described. Deduct 5 points if atlas registration or the source of spatial coordinates is not described. Deduct 4 points if consistency across three fish is not mentioned. Deduct 5 points if color intensity is interpreted as calcium activity or behavioral correlation.

Scoring items.criterion: Preserves the core conclusion for the eomesa-pvalb7 co-expressing population: the co-expressing cells are concentrated in the dorsolateral pallium and are consistent with the interpretation of a mammalian hippocampus-homologous region, indicating that this gene combination provides a localizable and targetable molecular entry point to the zebrafish hippocampus-homologous region.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct full points if the dorsolateral-pallium localization of co-expressing cells is not identified. Deduct 15 points if the response only states that the points are concentrated in a region but does not mention the hippocampus-homology meaning. Deduct full points if the co-expressing population is localized to the cerebellum, hindbrain, or whole brain. Deduct 6 points if the hippocampus-homology relationship is described as a completely new conclusion proven by this figure alone, rather than as consistent with existing evidence.

Scoring items.criterion: Preserves the region-specific conclusion for pvalb7: pvalb7-positive cells appear both along the lateral edge of the dorsal pallium and in cerebellar cells corresponding to known Purkinje cells; this dual localization shows that the same molecular marker can label specialized neuronal populations in different anatomical regions.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 12 points if the cerebellar pvalb7-positive cells are not identified as Purkinje cells. Deduct 8 points if the cerebellar distribution is described but the lateral dorsal-pallium distribution is omitted. Deduct full points if the cerebellar distribution is interpreted as nonspecific noise. Deduct 6 points if the biological meaning of the dual localization is not explained.

Scoring items.criterion: Places the figure in the overall logic of the study by stating that gene-expression combinations correspond to anatomical specialization and provide localization groundwork for later functional analysis of these molecular populations, while avoiding overinterpretation of spatial co-localization as functional causality or behavioral effect.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 5 points if the response does not state that the figure provides an anatomical anchor for later functional analysis. Deduct 5 points if it overstates the figure as proving the behavioral function or causal role of these cells. Deduct full points if it gives no broader biological interpretation and only lists the locations of the three panels.

Acceptable deviations: It is acceptable to describe the dorsolateral pallium as the dorsolateral telencephalic region or the zebrafish hippocampus-homologous region.
It is acceptable to describe Purkinje cells as cerebellar Purkinje cells.
It is acceptable to describe the RNA spot-count threshold as about 25 spots or the default positivity threshold.
It is acceptable to describe mapZebrain as a zebrafish reference brain atlas.
Omitting the exact color range of 1-148 is acceptable as long as color is not interpreted as functional activity.
It is acceptable to describe the views as dorsal and lateral views.
It is acceptable to state that the hippocampus-homology relationship is consistent with prior scRNA-seq or literature evidence.
rubric.Scoring instructions: High scores (85-100) require correctly reproducing the 3D spatial distributions and methodological sources for the three cell populations, accurately interpreting the hippocampus-homologous localization of the co-expressing population and the Purkinje-cell localization of pvalb7, and explaining that the figure provides molecular-anatomical correspondence rather than functional causal proof. Partial scores (40-84) should be assigned when the main locations are broadly correct but thresholds, atlas registration, hippocampus-homology meaning, or Purkinje-cell interpretation is incomplete. Low scores (0-39) should be assigned when the panel is confused with a functional activity map, the distributions of the three populations are mixed up, or no anatomical-specialization relationship is identified.
